title: A partner export API whose bulk customer files reach anyone who holds the link
provenance: Synthetic system authored for this corpus (issue #744). Not derived from, or sanitized from, any real system: there is nothing to leak by omission.
notes: Holdout case 3 for #744, written because cases 14 and 15 used all their HOLDOUT_READS. The corpus's first case where the system's purpose is to hand bulk personal data to third parties, so the worst findings are about where a finished file goes after a legitimate export: a signed download link that works for anyone who holds it, a webhook that carries that link to a callback URL the partner sets and the worker never checks, and a file store that keeps every file. The source states some controls (brand scope check, signed webhooks, single sign-on with a second factor), states some absences (plain-text client secrets that never expire, no export limit, no logging of scope changes or downloads, an audit table the admin console can edit), hedges one (the customers/orders scope check) and leaves others silent (job ownership on the status call, every internal connection, encryption at rest). ASVS level 2: the API releases customer names, email and postal addresses and order history to outside companies, which is the sensitive data level 2 is for; nothing states a demand that level 3 serves, such as payments or health data. Held out of tuning: no diagnosis reads it, so it confirms a fix measured on the other cases.
